fatal_errors: The proposed tungsten-alloying intervention does not reconstruct the target intervention of laser-assisted machining with localized preheating.
No specific baseline Ti-Ni-primary composition is given, so phase stability, tungsten solubility, and compliance with the 5–35 at% constraint cannot be verified.
The asserted tungsten strengthening and stable nanoprecipitate mechanisms are unsupported by cited prior evidence or phase-specific predictions.
The hypothesis predicts bulk yield-strength and creep improvements rather than the target outcomes of reduced cutting force, improved surface roughness, and reduced machining-induced work hardening.
Critical target process boundaries—localized heating to the softening regime, 0.3 mm cutting depth, removal of the heat-affected layer, and comparison with conventional machining—are absent.
explanation: The response is directionally aligned with the broad Ti/Ni-primary HEA and 800–1000 °C context, but it proposes an entirely different intervention and endpoint set. Its paired-alloy experiment is testable and includes a numerical falsification threshold, although the unspecified base composition, creep stress, exposure duration, replication, and statistical criterion limit discrimination. Most importantly, no supporting evidence is supplied, and the proposed lattice-distortion and nanoprecipitation mechanisms are speculative. Consequently, it is neither a reconstruction of the target nor a sufficiently evidenced alternative hypothesis.
